​2026 Bio-inspired Intelligence Global Summit held in Nanjing On November 12, the 2026 Bio-inspired Intelligence Global Summit was held in Nanjing. Tan Tieniu, Chair of Nanjing University CPC Council,  Academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and President of the World Data Organization; along with Mayor of Nanjing Li Zhongjun, attended and delivered speeches. Attendees also included CAS Academicians Chu Junhao, Huang Wei, Zhu Meifang, Hong Wei, Xing Dingyu, Zhu Shining, Gu Ning, Ma Yuqiang, Shi Yi, and Zheng Hairong, Academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering Wu Feng, and international expert in the field of smart biomedical devices, Mohamad Sawan. The theme of this conference was "Bio-inspired Intelligence Innovating the Future." Academicians from the two academies, experts from universities and research institutions, as well as representatives from industries and investment sectors were invited to gather in Nanjing. They engaged in discussions and exchanges around the scientific mechanisms, key technologies, and industrial pathways of bio-intelligence. The event showcased new technologies, products, and enterprises emerging in the field of bio-intelligence, striving to foster a new ecology for the future industry of bio-intelligence. Mayor Li Zhongjun stated that as a key hub of the Yangtze River Delta International Science and Innovation Center, Nanjing boasts a fertile environment for talent development, a strong industrial foundation, and vibrant capital. Equipped with favorable conditions for deploying the field of bio-intelligence, the city will earnestly implement the key messages from General Secretary Xi Jinping's speech on advancing cutting-edge industrial layouts and development. Nanjing aims to promote the deep integration of technological innovation and industrial advancement, positioning itself as a source for disruptive innovation, the preferred destination for high-value outcomes, and a hub for futuristic industries. Nanjing will extend the utmost sincerity, offer optimal services, and create the best environment to provide a broad platform for universities and research institutes to focus on innovation, for patient investors to invest freely, and for enterprises to grow robustly. Tan Tieniu explained that global innovation in artificial intelligence technology is currently experiencing an unprecedented period of activity. As a significant force in the national strategies for science and technology innovation, NJU boasts extensive experience and unique strengths in developing bio-inspired AI and human-machine collaborative intelligence. He expressed hopes that the conference would serve as a pivotal opportunity to strengthen close collaborations among universities, research institutes, leading enterprises, and local governments, deepen interdisciplinary research, and jointly propel bio-inspired intelligent technologies from scientific frontiers into industrial practice. This would facilitate the integration of key links in the industrial chain and optimize the allocation of resources, ultimately building a globally competitive smart industry ecosystem. During the conference, the NJU Bio-inspired Intelligence Research Institute was officially inaugurated. The institute will focus on four major research directions: fundamentals and large models of bio-inspired intelligence, bio-inspired perception and computation, bio-computing and organoid intelligence, and bio-agents and embodied systems. Relying on NJU's academic and talent advantages and the industrial scenarios provided by Xuanwu District, Nanjing, the institute aims to establish itself as an originator of foundational innovation and a leading hub for future industries in the field of bio-intelligence. The conference also witnessed the launch of NJU's first set of bio-inspired intelligence projects, the interdisciplinary program of "Bio-inspired Intelligence Science and Technology," and a global recruitment initiative. Additionally, ceremonies were held to inaugurate the Bio-inspired Intelligence Industrial Fund, Bio-inspired Intelligence Innovation Workshop, and the establishment of the Bio-Intelligence Science and Technology Innovation Alliance. During the keynote speech session,  Chinese and foreign academicians and experts addressed the core focuses of bio-intelligence, analyzed key challenges, and clarified development pathways, providing forward-looking insights for technological evolution and industrial applications. Zheng Hairong,  Academician of the CAS, Executive Vice President of NJU, and Director of the National High-Performance Medical Device Innovation Center, also delivered a presentation on bio-inspired intelligence. The conference also featured themed industrial keynote speeches, roundtable forums, and roadshows of emerging future entities. Deputy Secretary-General of Jiangsu Provincial Government and Director of the General Office Qiu Zhiqiang, Deputy Director of the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Industry and Information Technology Chi Yu, Secretary of Xuanwu District Party Committee of Nanjing City Zhang Zhichao, and relevant officials from city and district departments, as well as representatives from universities, research institutions, industry enterprises, and investment organizations, attended the conference.
